Japan from the Meiji Restoration of 1868 to the present: first an empire that industrialised and conquered, then, after defeat in 1945, a democracy and one of the world's largest economies.

Empire (1868 to 1945). Under the Meiji Emperor Japan built railways, schools, factories and a conscript army, and adopted the Meiji Constitution in 1889. It beat China in 1895, taking Taiwan, and Russia in 1905, and annexed Korea in 1910. In the 1920s it had party governments and growing cities, but after 1931 the army took Manchuria and gained control at home. War with China from 1937 and with the United States from the attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941 brought Japan into the Second World War. It ended with firebombing, the atomic bombings and surrender in August 1945.

Since 1945. The American occupation, which lasted until 1952, rewrote the rules:

  • The Constitution of 1947 gave power to the people, renounced war and made the emperor a symbol.
  • Land reform broke up big estates, and women got the vote.

Then came fast growth. Companies such as Toyota and Sony led exports, the Shinkansen opened in 1964, and by the late 1960s Japan's economy was second only to America's. The asset bubble burst around 1990, and slow growth followed for decades. Since 2008 the population has been shrinking and ageing faster than almost anywhere. The 2011 Tohoku earthquake and tsunami and nuclear disaster were the worst shock since the war. Japan remains a major economy and a cultural force, from anime to food.
sum: Japan from the Meiji Restoration of 1868 to the present: first an empire that industrialised and conquered, then, after defeat in 1945, a democracy and one of the world's largest economies.
